ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached image shows two small-molecule space-filling models of similar size displayed side by side, indicating that the objects being compared are two comparable small molecules. The textual formulas given in the question stem indicate that the substances compared on the left/right are ethanoic acid (CH3COOH, carboxylic acid) and ethanol (CH3CH2OH, alcohol). Reasoning: Both ethanol and ethanoic acid contain O-H, and both can form hydrogen bonds, so the key reason ethanoic acid has a lower vapor pressure is not merely "having O-H". Stronger intermolecular attractions make ethanoic acid molecules less likely to escape into the gas phase, so the vapor pressure of ethanoic acid is significantly lower than that of ethanol.

method.method_draft: First describe the image as showing two comparable small molecular models. Compare their intermolecular forces: both can hydrogen bond, so the key difference is not merely the presence of an O-H group. Ethanoic acid’s carboxyl group allows stronger, more extensive hydrogen bonding than ethanol, often forming acid dimers. Stronger attractions reduce the tendency of molecules to escape into the gas phase, so ethanoic acid has the lower vapor pressure.
